Ectopic adrenal myelolipoma at the hepatic-adrenal interface mimicking hepatic angiomyolipoma: A case report
abstract: BACKGROUND Myelolipoma is an extremely rare benign tumor composed of mature adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements. Its non-specific clinical presentation and imaging characteristics make preoperative diagnosis difficult, and it may be misdiagnosed as other fat-containing hepatic tumors, particularly hepatic angiomyolipoma. The tissue origin and pathogenesis of hepatic myelolipoma remain unclear. This report presents a rare case of an ectopic adrenal myelolipoma located at the hepatic-adrenal interface with liver involvement. CASE SUMMARY A 61-year-old woman presented with intermittent right upper abdominal pain for more than 2 months. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 6.2 cm × 4.2 cm fat-containing mass in the right posterior liver adjacent to the right adrenal gland. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked signal loss on opposed-phase images, mild delayed enhancement, and hypointensity in the hepatobiliary phase. Hepatic angiomyolipoma was suspected preoperatively. Given the patient’s symptoms and the lesion’s size (> 6 cm), laparoscopic local resection of the right posterior liver was performed. Histopathological examination showed mature adipose and hematopoietic tissues within the capsule, focal adrenal tissue immediately inside the capsule, and hepatic tissue outside the capsule. These findings supported a diagnosis of ectopic adrenal myelolipoma with liver involvement. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 7. During 19 months of follow-up, her abdominal pain improved, with no documented recurrence or postoperative complications. CONCLUSION Ectopic adrenal myelolipoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of fat-containing lesions at the hepatic-adrenal interface.

title: A framework for outpatient CAR-T monitoring to support Canadian CAR-T capacity building
abstract: Introduction: why outpatient CAR-T therapy now in Canada? Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has significantly improved outcomes, including sustained remissions and even cures, for patients with refractory or relapsed B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), and multiple myeloma (MM).1-8 CAR-T products differ by antigen target, such as CD19 and B cell maturation antigen (BCMA); and by co-stimulatory domain, which is either CD28 (e.g., axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel) or 4-1BB (e.g., tisagenlecleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel). Prior to CAR-T availability, patients with relapsed hematologic malignancies experienced poor outcomes. For example, in patients with relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphomas, the median overall survival was 6.2 months. prior to access to CAR-T therapy.9 These outcomes are balanced by CAR-T therapy-associated toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS). Despite the substantial clinical benefits observed with CAR T-cell therapy, treatment is associated with distinct immune-mediated toxicities, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity (ICANs). Although these adverse events are generally manageable with established treatment algorithms and are often reversible, severe toxicities, resulting in organ dysfunction and occasionally death, may occur and can necessitate ICU-level care. Enhanced understanding of toxicity kinetics, earlier intervention strategies, and the availability of effective management approaches such as tocilizumab and corticosteroids have improved the safety profile of CAR T-cell therapy. Early interventions, such as tocilizumab (anti-IL-6R) and corticosteroids, can attenuate the severity of these toxicities. Given the potential for severe toxicities, CAR-T has traditionally been administered and monitored in an inpatient hospital setting.

title: The burden of disease for children diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome — a European cohort study
abstract: Background Klinefelter syndrome is a congenital chromosomal anomaly, where males have an extra X-chromosome. The syndrome may be associated with hypergonadotropic hypogonadism and many are late or undiagnosed. This European, population-based data-linkage cohort study was part of the EUROlinkCAT project and investigated the burden of disease for the first ten years of life for European children diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome. Results Thirteen national and regional population-based registries in ten countries from the European surveillance of congenital anomalies (EUROCAT) network participated. Data for live born children born in 1995-2014 and diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome prenatally or during infancy were linked to mortality and hospital records. Data for liveborn children born with any congenital anomaly and children without a congenital anomaly (reference children) were included for comparison on morbidity. Out of 5.8 million live born children 278 were diagnosed with Klinefelter syndrome in the 13 registry areas, 96.8% survived the first 5 year of life, 64.7% (95% CI 51.8;75.0) were admitted to hospital during the first year with a median length of stay of 3.9 (95% CI 3.0;4.7) days, 10.8% (95% CI 6.9;16.4) had a hospital stay of ≥10 days and 12.3% (95% CI 7.1;18.9) underwent surgery. In the age group 1-4 years of age 53.5% (95% CI 41.2;64.4) were admitted to hospital, the median length of stay decreased to 0.7 (95% CI 0.3;1.1) days and 6.3% (95% CI 2.6;12.3) had a hospital stay of ≥ 10 days. Conclusions More children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome were hospitalised and underwent more surgery compared to reference children, while less were hospitalised and fewer had surgery than all children with any other congenital anomaly. Thus, the burden of disease was increased for children diagnosed prenatally or in infancy with Klinefelter syndrome but decreased overall after the first year of life.

title: Superyacht charter in Greece: seasons, demand and pricing outlook for 2027
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Greece is the largest single destination in the global superyacht charter market. This report reviews public sources published up to 23 November 2026 to describe the seasons, demand and cost structure of crewed superyacht charter in Greece, and to set out what the evidence suggests for 2027. Industry booking data put Greece at 27% of summer 2026 bookings for yachts of 20 metres and over, unchanged from 2025, and at 32% of the market between May and October. Greek associations, however, describe a divided 2026 season: a trade body reported stable charter numbers and higher total charter value, with growth at the top of the market, while a crew union reported that motor yacht activity fell by at least 25% after early-season bookings collapsed. Both describe a shift towards last-minute booking. Worldwide, advance bookings for 2027 were 13% below the previous year's position at the end of October 2026, but booked days were less than 2% lower because average charter length rose from 9.4 to 10.7 days. On cost, Greece applies a 13% VAT rate to crewed charters of more than 48 hours, with certificate-based reductions that lead to effective rates of 5.2% or 6.5%. We conclude that demand for the larger end of the Greek market looks resilient into 2027, that pricing at the top is likely to hold, and that booking windows will stay unusually wide, with late decisions sitting alongside early commitments for the longest and largest charters. Published by Oxyzen Yachting, Athens, Greece: https://www.oxyzenyachting.com/

title: Batas Kewajiban Melestarikan Tradisi Lokal bagi Santri Nusantara dalam Perspektif Kaidah Al-'Adah Muhakkamah Ditinjau Berdasarkan Tradisi Masyarakat dan Syariat
journal: Sujud: Jurnal Agama, Sosial dan Budaya
abstract: Local traditions constitute an important part of the social identity and cultural heritage of Indonesian society, including the lives of santri and Islamic boarding schools. These traditions are often regarded as ancestral legacies that should be preserved to maintain cultural continuity. However, the assumption that every tradition must always be preserved requires critical examination, particularly when cultural preservation is considered an obligation. This study aims to analyze the limits of the obligation to preserve local traditions among Indonesian santri through the perspectives of the Islamic legal maxim al-'adah muhakkamah, the concepts of 'urf shahih and 'urf fasid, and the relationship between Islam and local culture. This research employs a qualitative library research method by examining scholarly literature, legal regulations, and studies on local cultural practices. The discussion demonstrates that traditions hold significant social value, yet they should not be preserved without critical evaluation. The legal maxim al-'adah muhakkamah recognizes customary practices as a consideration in Islamic law as long as they meet the requirements of Sharia. Furthermore, the constitutional right to maintain cultural heritage cannot automatically be interpreted as a religious obligation to preserve every customary practice. This study argues that cultural preservation should be based on public benefit, conformity with Islamic principles, and consideration of its social consequences. Therefore, santri should develop a critical and selective attitude toward preserving the cultural heritage of the Nusantara.

title: Predictive value of bone mineral density assessment methods for postoperative complications after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
journal: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
abstract: Objective To investigate the predictive value of preoperative bone mineral density (BMD) measurements for postoperative complications and reoperation risk in patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA). Methods A total of 1,945 patients with knee osteoarthritis (KOA) who underwent primary UKA at the Affiliated Hospital of Jining Medical University between November 2018 and November 2025 were retrospectively included. Preoperative lumbar spine BMD was measured using quantitative computed tomography. Patients were divided into a reduced BMD group (< 80 mg/cm³) and a normal BMD group (≥ 80 mg/cm³). Data on demographics, surgical parameters, and outcomes were collected. Propensity score matching was performed to balance confounding variables. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were conducted to identify independent risk factors for postoperative complications, and receiver operating characteristic curves were plotted to evaluate the predictive efficacy of BMD. Results Among the enrolled patients, 234 (12.03%) were in the reduced BMD group and 1,711 (87.97%) in the normal BMD group, with the former having a higher proportion of women patients and a higher age (P < 0.001). After 1:1 propensity score matching, 233 patients remained in each group. The reoperation rate was significantly higher in the reduced BMD group (3.00% vs. 0.43%, P = 0.032). Patients with complications had a significantly lower median lumbar BMD value compared with those without complications (93.3 vs. 103.2 mg/cm³, P = 0.026). Multivariate logistic regression analysis confirmed that lumbar BMD was an independent negative predictor of complications after UKA ( OR = 0.700, P = 0.007); lower BMD values were associated with higher risks of postoperative complications. Conclusions Preoperative decreased BMD is an independent risk factor for postoperative complications and reoperation after UKA. Routine preoperative BMD screening and optimized perioperative bone health management should be implemented to reduce complications and improve surgical outcomes.
